themes_detail.label: Food Safety Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Food establishment complaints surged to 7 this week versus a 1.9 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 273% spike (z-score: 5.53)—suggesting either a new inspection wave or emerging food safety violations in CD 408 restaurants and vendors.
evidence: 7 food establishment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly baseline (8-week average)
273% increase with z-score of 5.53 (statistically significant anomaly)
Signal appeared in most recent reporting period; not a lagged or historical spike
reporting_angles: Which restaurants or food vendors are generating the complaints? Are they concentrated in one neighborhood area?
Interview DOH inspector or restaurant owners about what violations are driving the surge—is it a seasonal pattern or new problem?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Fireworks in Peak Week
themes_detail.summary: Illegal fireworks complaints hit 23 three weeks ago, a 1,433% spike from the 1.5 weekly average (z-score: 6.56), indicating a discrete event or sustained illegal activity that warrants follow-up to see if this persists into the present week.
evidence: 23 illegal fireworks complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.5 weekly baseline (8-week average)
1,433% increase with z-score of 6.56 (very high statistical significance)
Spike is time-bound; current status unclear—needs reporting to determine if ongoing
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD about enforcement actions and which neighborhoods were hotspots for illegal fireworks
Document resident complaints and safety concerns; investigate whether fireworks activity has resumed this week

themes_detail.label: Asbestos Discovery or Inspections
themes_detail.summary: Asbestos complaints jumped to 5 three weeks ago, a 1,900% spike from the 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 10.97), suggesting either recent building demolitions/renovations triggering inspections or a contamination incident in the district.
evidence: 5 asbestos complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly baseline (8-week average)
1,900% increase with z-score of 10.97 (extremely high statistical significance)
662 DOB permits filed in last 90 days (394 alterations, 17 full demolitions) could indicate construction triggering asbestos disclosure
reporting_angles: Cross-reference asbestos complaints with DOB demolition and alteration permits filed 3-4 weeks ago—which buildings are involved?
Interview affected residents and DOH/DOB officials about remediation status and health impacts

themes_detail.label: Park Noise Complaints Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints spiked to 4 three weeks ago, a 3,100% jump from the 0.1 weekly average (z-score: 11.72)—the single largest anomaly in the dataset—indicating a severe, concentrated disruption (likely events, gatherings, or construction) that may have already resolved or be ongoing.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly baseline (8-week average)
3,100% increase with z-score of 11.72 (highest statistical anomaly in entire dataset)
Community Board budget requests include park reconstruction/upgrades; suggests facilities maintenance issues may be related
reporting_angles: Which parks generated the complaints? Were special events, concerts, or construction projects scheduled 3 weeks ago?
Check with Parks Department on current noise-generating activities and whether the issue has been resolved

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicle Cleanup Gap
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints reached 21 two weeks ago, a 154% spike from the 8.2 weekly average (z-score: 3.01), suggesting neighborhood streets are accumulating abandoned cars faster than the city is removing them.
evidence: 21 derelict vehicle complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 8.2 weekly baseline (8-week average)
Complements long-running illegal parking problem (2,168 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Identify streets with the highest derelict vehicle concentration; map against illegal parking hotspots
Interview NYPD or Sanitation about removal timelines and capacity constraints
